_comment: The wasmer-gui guest API. Everything else is generated from this file by codegen/gen.py:
the C header, the host's Rust readers and import glue, the page-side JavaScript tables and the layout checks.
The schema follows webgpu-headers' webgpu.json (enums, bitflags, structs, objects with methods), plus `events`.
Rules the generator enforces: results are a status, nothing, or one of the two listed exceptions;
imports take scalars and pointers only; event records use fixed-width fields only.
name: gui
doc:
Windows, input, text entry and the clipboard for WASIX programs.

A program creates an instance, opens windows on it, and drains the instance's event queue. The host never calls into the program: everything it has to say arrives as an event record, and everything a platform wants answered on the spot is declared ahead of time.

Every function returns a WGUIStatus (or nothing) and hands values back through out-pointers. A host that does not have a function answers WGUIStatus_Unimplemented and does nothing, so a program built against a newer header still starts on an older host.

All functions may be called from any thread. Sizes and positions are physical pixels unless stated otherwise.

constants.name: abi_version
constants.doc: The version of this header: major << 16 | minor. WGUI_INSTANCE_DESCRIPTOR_INIT passes it to the host, which behaves as that version describes.

constants.name: max_event_size
constants.doc: No event record is larger. A buffer handed to wguiInstancePollEvents must hold at least this many bytes.

constants.name: strlen
constants.doc: As a string length: the string is NUL-terminated.

constants.name: position_undefined
constants.doc: A window position the host does not know or does not tell (Wayland, a browser).

constants.name: no_text_cursor
constants.doc: As a composition's selection: the input method shows no cursor.

constants.name: stype_must_understand
constants.doc: Set in a chained struct's sType when ignoring it would be wrong. A host that does not know the struct then fails the call with WGUIStatus_Unsupported instead of skipping it.

constants.name: key_tag_mask
constants.doc: The part of a WGUIKey that says what the rest means.

constants.name: key_value_mask
constants.doc: The part of a WGUIKey its tag describes.

constants.name: key_character
constants.doc: Tag: the value is the one Unicode scalar value the key produces (0 is WGUIKey_Unidentified).

constants.name: key_named
constants.doc: Tag: a named key, one of the WGUIKey_* constants.

constants.name: key_dead
constants.doc: Tag: a dead key. The value is the combining character it adds to the next key, or 0 if unknown.

constants.name: key_sequence
constants.doc: Tag: the key produces more than one scalar value. The value is the first; the event's keyString has all of them.

constants.name: pointer_id_mouse
constants.doc: The pointer id of the mouse cursor, whichever mouse or touchpad moves it.

objects.name: instance
objects.doc: A program's connection to the window system, and its event queue. Destroying it destroys its windows and cursors.

methods.name: destroy
methods.doc: Destroys the instance with everything created on it. Requests still pending complete as WGUIStatus_Cancelled and are then dropped with the queue.

methods.name: get_info
methods.doc: What kind of host this is and what it has.

methods.name: poll_events
methods.doc:
Copies queued event records into `buffer`, oldest first, as many whole records as fit, and sets `written` to their total size (0 when the queue is empty). Never blocks.

`buffer` must be 8-byte aligned and `capacity` at least WGUI_MAX_EVENT_SIZE, so one record always fits. Step through the records with wguiEventFirst and wguiEventNext.

This call and wguiInstanceWaitEvents are also where signals reach the program. A WASIX runtime delivers them where a program enters the system, and a program that draws frame after frame may do that nowhere else, so the host lets them in here: a handler the program installed runs before the call returns, and a signal that ends the program ends it in this call.

methods.name: wait_events
methods.doc:
Blocks until the queue has a record, wguiInstanceWake is called, or `timeout` nanoseconds pass (0 only checks; WGUI_WAIT_FOREVER never times out). `reasons` says why it returned; 0 is a timeout.

A wake that happened before the wait is not lost: it ends the next wait. Signals reach the program as this call returns, not while it sleeps in it (see wguiInstancePollEvents). So that they are not kept waiting, the host ends a long wait early with WGUIWaitReasons_Interrupted: unless a signal handler did something, nothing happened, and the program waits again.

methods.name: wake
methods.doc: Ends the current wguiInstanceWaitEvents of this instance, or the next one if none is waiting. For waking a program's event loop from another thread.

methods.name: set_event_mask
methods.doc: Chooses which classes of events are queued from now on. Records already queued stay. WGUIEventClass_System cannot be turned off.

methods.name: get_time
methods.doc: The current time on the clock event timestamps use, in nanoseconds. Hosts make it the WASI monotonic clock where they can.

methods.name: get_displays
methods.doc: Lists the displays, the primary one first. Writes up to `capacity` handles and sets `count` to how many there are. Display handles stay valid until WGUIEventType_DisplaysChanged says the set changed.

methods.name: create_window
methods.doc:
Opens a window, or adopts the target the descriptor names. NULL asks for the host's default window.

The first record queued for the new window is a WGUIEventType_WindowResized with its real size and scale factor.

methods.name: create_cursor
methods.doc: Makes a cursor from an image, for wguiWindowSetCustomCursor.

methods.name: get_clipboard_info
methods.doc: What the host knows about a clipboard right now, without reading it.

methods.name: read_clipboard
methods.doc:
Copies the clipboard's content of one MIME type into `buffer` and sets `size` to its length in bytes. Text is "text/plain", UTF-8, not NUL-terminated.

WGUIStatus_BufferTooSmall: `size` holds what is needed, nothing was copied. WGUIStatus_Pending: the host cannot answer without asking the system first (a browser); call wguiInstanceRequestClipboard and read again once it completes. WGUIStatus_NotFound: nothing of that type. WGUIStatus_Denied: the program may not read the clipboard.

methods.name: request_clipboard
methods.doc: Asks the host to fetch the clipboard's content of one MIME type, so that wguiInstanceReadClipboard can answer. Completes with WGUIEventType_RequestCompleted carrying `tag`: Success, Denied or NotFound.

methods.name: write_clipboard
methods.doc: Replaces the clipboard's content with these items (one per MIME type; none clears it). The program's own reads see the new content at once; WGUIEventType_RequestCompleted with `tag` says whether the system took it.

objects.name: display
objects.doc: A screen. Displays belong to the host: there is nothing to destroy.

methods.name: get_info
methods.doc: The display's geometry, scale factor and refresh rate.

methods.name: get_name
methods.doc: The display's name for people, UTF-8, not NUL-terminated. Copies up to `capacity` bytes and sets `length` to the name's full length.

objects.name: window
objects.doc: A window: a native top-level window, or a target the embedder provides (a canvas in a browser, a view in an app).

methods.name: destroy
methods.doc: Closes the window. No more records are queued for it; ones already queued can still be read. A WebGPU surface created on it keeps presenting nowhere until it is released.

methods.name: get_state
methods.doc: The window's current size, scale factor, position and flags. Answered from what the host last saw, without waiting for the window system.

methods.name: get_surface_selector
methods.doc:
The name to draw on this window with WebGPU: put it in WGPUWasixSurfaceSourceCanvas.selector. UTF-8, not NUL-terminated. Copies up to `capacity` bytes and sets `length` to the full length.

For a window that adopted a named target this is that name; otherwise the host makes one up, starting with "wgui:".

methods.name: set_title
methods.doc: Sets the window's title.

methods.name: set_size
methods.doc: Asks for a new size of the content area. The size the window ends up with arrives as WGUIEventType_WindowResized; WGUIStatus_Unsupported when the embedder decides the size.

methods.name: set_size_limits
methods.doc: Limits how small and how large the user can make the content area. 0 means no limit.

methods.name: set_position
methods.doc: Moves the window's content area to a position on the desktop. Needs WGUIFeatureName_WindowPosition.

methods.name: set_flags
methods.doc: Changes the flags in `mask` to their bits in `values`: show or hide, minimize, maximize, restore, borders, level. What actually happened arrives as WGUIEventType_WindowFlagsChanged. `unsupported` receives the bits of `mask` this host cannot change.

methods.name: set_fullscreen
methods.doc:
Enters fullscreen as `options` says, or leaves it when `options` is NULL. Completes with WGUIEventType_RequestCompleted carrying `tag`. Where the platform insists on a user gesture (a browser), the request waits for the next one unless the options forbid waiting.

The user can leave fullscreen without the program asking; WGUIEventType_WindowFlagsChanged reports every change.

methods.name: focus
methods.doc: Asks for keyboard focus and brings the window forward. Window systems may refuse.

methods.name: request_attention
methods.doc: Asks for the user's attention without taking focus (a bouncing icon, a flashing task bar entry).

methods.name: request_redraw
methods.doc: Asks for one WGUIEventType_WindowRedrawRequested, which comes when the display is ready for the window's next frame: a program that draws whenever it is told to and asks again runs at the display's pace. Several requests before it is delivered make one event; none is delivered while the window cannot be seen.

methods.name: set_cursor_shape
methods.doc: Shows one of the system's cursors over the window.

methods.name: set_custom_cursor
methods.doc: Shows a cursor made with wguiInstanceCreateCursor over the window.

methods.name: set_cursor_visible
methods.doc: Shows or hides the cursor while it is over the window.

methods.name: set_cursor_grab
methods.doc:
Keeps the cursor inside the window (Confined), or hides it and reports only movement (Locked), or lets it go (None). Completes with WGUIEventType_RequestCompleted carrying `tag`; a later request cancels one still pending.

A grab is lent, not owned: the user or the system can end it, and WGUIEventType_WindowCursorGrabChanged reports every change. The host never gives one kind of grab in place of another.

methods.name: set_cursor_position
methods.doc: Moves the cursor to a position in the window. Needs WGUIFeatureName_CursorWarp.

methods.name: set_text_input
methods.doc: Starts text entry in this window, or updates it (call again whenever the caret moves), or stops it with NULL. While it is on, input methods and on-screen keyboards work, and every insertion arrives as WGUIEventType_TextCommit.

methods.name: reset_text_input
methods.doc: Throws away the text being composed, as when the program moves its caret itself.

methods.name: set_default_actions
methods.doc: Says which of the embedder's own reactions to input the host should prevent while this window has it (a browser scrolling the page on a wheel turn or on the space bar, its context menu). A program polls for input and cannot refuse an event in time, so it states its choice ahead. Hosts without such reactions accept and ignore it.

methods.name: present_pixels
methods.doc:
Shows a frame the program drew itself: for programs without a GPU (WGUIFeatureName_PixelPresent). The frame is copied before the call returns, so the program can draw the next one into the same memory.

The frame fills the window. One of another size than the window's is scaled to it, which a program avoids by drawing at the size the last WGUIEventType_WindowResized told. `damage` lists the rectangles of the frame that differ from the one presented before; none means all of it. A host may show more than what is listed, never less.

The call does not wait for the display. A program that animates asks for wguiWindowRequestRedraw after each frame and draws the next one when WGUIEventType_WindowRedrawRequested comes, which is once per refresh of the display; frames presented faster than they can be shown replace each other. A window is drawn this way or through a WebGPU surface, not both.

methods.name: destroy
methods.doc: Destroys the cursor. Windows showing it go back to the default cursor.

functions.name: get_version
functions.doc: The newest version of this API the host implements, as major << 16 | minor. 0 means the host has no such function (it is older than every version).

functions.name: has_feature
functions.doc: Whether this program may use a feature here: the host can do it and the embedder allows it.

functions.name: get_features
functions.doc: Lists the features wguiHasFeature would confirm. Writes up to `capacity` of them and sets `count` to how many there are.

functions.name: create_instance
functions.doc: Connects to the window system. NULL is WGUI_INSTANCE_DESCRIPTOR_INIT. Fails with WGUIStatus_Unsupported when a required feature is missing.

enums.name: status
enums.doc: What a function did. Out-values are written only on Success, unless a status says otherwise.

entries.name: unimplemented
entries.doc: The host does not have this function. Nothing was done and nothing was written.

entries.name: success
entries.doc: Done, or the request was accepted.

entries.name: error
entries.doc: The host failed.

entries.name: unsupported
entries.doc: The host knows this, but cannot do it here: the platform lacks it or the feature is not enabled.

entries.name: invalid_argument
entries.doc: An enum value, a struct, a chain, a string that is not UTF-8, a missing pointer, or a reserved field that is not zero.

entries.name: invalid_handle
entries.doc: A handle that is null, stale or of another type.

entries.name: buffer_too_small
entries.doc: The size needed was written; nothing else was.

entries.name: pending
entries.doc: The answer needs a request first.

entries.name: denied
entries.doc: The user, a permission or the embedder's policy said no.

entries.name: limit_exceeded
entries.doc: A limit set by the embedder was reached.

entries.name: not_found
entries.doc: No such target, or nothing of that type.

entries.name: busy
entries.doc: The target is already in use by another window.

entries.name: lost
entries.doc: The window's host side is gone.

entries.name: cancelled
entries.doc: A request was replaced by a later one, or what it was for was destroyed.

enums.name: s_type
enums.doc: Identifies a struct in a nextInChain list. This version defines none; hosts skip the ones they do not know unless WGUI_STYPE_MUST_UNDERSTAND is set.

entries.name: invalid
entries.doc: Not a struct type.

enums.name: feature_name
enums.doc: Something a host may or may not offer. Query with wguiHasFeature.

entries.name: windows
entries.doc: Windows can be created at all.

entries.name: top_level_windows
entries.doc: Windows beyond the targets the embedder provides: real top-level windows, as many as the embedder's limit allows.

entries.name: window_position
entries.doc: Window positions are known and can be set.

entries.name: window_states
entries.doc: Minimize, maximize, borders and level can be changed.

entries.name: fullscreen_borderless
entries.doc: Fullscreen at the display's own mode.

entries.name: fullscreen_exclusive
entries.doc: Fullscreen with a display mode of the program's choice.

entries.name: displays
entries.doc: Displays are listed with real geometry.

entries.name: text_input
entries.doc: Input methods: composition and committed text.

entries.name: screen_keyboard
entries.doc: An on-screen keyboard can be shown and hidden.

entries.name: touch
entries.doc: Touch contacts are reported as pointers.

entries.name: pen
entries.doc: Pens are reported as pointers, with pressure and tilt where the hardware has them.

entries.name: raw_input
entries.doc: The WGUIEventClass_Raw events.

entries.name: raw_input_unfocused
entries.doc: Raw events arrive while no window of the program has focus.

entries.name: cursor_shapes
entries.doc: wguiWindowSetCursorShape.

entries.name: custom_cursors
entries.doc: wguiInstanceCreateCursor.

entries.name: cursor_warp
entries.doc: wguiWindowSetCursorPosition.

entries.name: cursor_confine
entries.doc: WGUICursorGrab_Confined.

entries.name: cursor_lock
entries.doc: WGUICursorGrab_Locked.

entries.name: clipboard_text
entries.doc: Text can be written to the clipboard, and read if the embedder allows.

entries.name: clipboard_sync_read
entries.doc: wguiInstanceReadClipboard never answers WGUIStatus_Pending.

entries.name: theme
entries.doc: Light or dark appearance is known.

entries.name: attention_request
entries.doc: wguiWindowRequestAttention.

entries.name: clipboard_data
entries.doc: Reserved: clipboard content other than text.

entries.name: primary_selection
entries.doc: Reserved: WGUIClipboardSelection_Primary.

entries.name: gestures
entries.doc: Reserved: pinch, rotate and pan gestures.

entries.name: keyboard_layout
entries.doc: Reserved: the layout's key map.

entries.name: text_surrounding
entries.doc: Reserved: text around the caret for input methods.

entries.name: drag_and_drop
entries.doc: Reserved: dragging to and from windows.

entries.name: pixel_present
entries.doc: wguiWindowPresentPixels: showing frames the program drew itself, without a GPU.

entries.name: event_fd
entries.doc: Reserved: a file descriptor that becomes readable when events are queued.

entries.name: gamepads
entries.doc: Reserved: game controllers.

enums.name: host_kind
enums.doc: What is behind the window system.

entries.name: headless
entries.doc: No screen: windows exist, and input comes from whoever embeds the program.

entries.name: desktop
entries.doc: A desktop window system.

entries.name: browser
entries.doc: A web page: windows are canvases.

entries.name: mobile
entries.doc: A phone or tablet.

entries.name: embedded
entries.doc: Views inside another application.

entries.name: fullscreen
entries.doc: wguiWindowSetFullscreen

entries.name: cursor_grab
entries.doc: wguiWindowSetCursorGrab

entries.name: clipboard_request
entries.doc: wguiInstanceRequestClipboard

entries.name: clipboard_write
entries.doc: wguiInstanceWriteClipboard

entries.name: none
entries.doc: Not fullscreen.

entries.name: borderless
entries.doc: The window covers the display at its current mode.

entries.name: exclusive
entries.doc: The display switches mode for the window. Needs WGUIFeatureName_FullscreenExclusive.

entries.name: none
entries.doc: Stop asking.

entries.name: informational
entries.doc: Once, gently.

entries.name: critical
entries.doc: Until the user responds.

entries.name: none
entries.doc: The cursor is free.

entries.name: confined
entries.doc: The cursor stays inside the window.

entries.name: locked
entries.doc: The cursor is hidden and stays where it was. Pointer events keep that position and carry the movement in deltaX and deltaY.

enums.name: cursor_grab_reason
enums.doc: Why a window's cursor grab changed.

entries.name: requested
entries.doc: The program asked.

entries.name: user
entries.doc: The user ended it (Escape in a browser).

entries.name: focus_lost
entries.doc: The window lost focus. The host grabs again when focus returns.

entries.name: focus_gained
entries.doc: The grab came back with focus.

entries.name: host
entries.doc: The host or the embedder took it away.

enums.name: cursor_shape
enums.doc: The system's cursors, named as in CSS.

entries.name: clipboard
entries.doc: What copy and paste use.

entries.name: primary
entries.doc: The selection X11 and Wayland paste with the middle button. Needs WGUIFeatureName_PrimarySelection.

enums.name: text_input_purpose
enums.doc: What a text field is for. Hosts use it to choose a keyboard and to switch helpers off.

entries.name: auto
entries.doc: Shown when there is no hardware keyboard.

enums.name: key_location
enums.doc: Which of several keys with the same meaning.

entries.name: mouse
entries.doc: The mouse cursor: every mouse and touchpad together, always pointer id WGUI_POINTER_ID_MOUSE.

entries.name: touch
entries.doc: One finger. Its id lasts from WGUIEventType_PointerDown to PointerUp or PointerCancel.

entries.name: pen
entries.doc: A pen. Its id lasts from PointerEnter to PointerLeave.

enums.name: pointer_button
enums.doc: Values above Forward are further buttons of the device, numbered on.

entries.name: none
entries.doc: No button changed (motion, enter, leave).

entries.name: primary
entries.doc: The left mouse button, a touch contact, a pen's tip.

entries.name: secondary
entries.doc: The right mouse button, a pen's barrel button.

entries.name: auxiliary
entries.doc: The middle mouse button.

entries.name: eraser
entries.doc: A pen's eraser end.

entries.name: line
entries.doc: Notches of a wheel.

entries.name: pixel
entries.doc: Physical pixels, from a touchpad or a precise wheel.

enums.name: wheel_phase
enums.doc: Where a wheel record stands in a scroll gesture.

entries.name: none
entries.doc: A plain wheel: no gesture.

enums.name: pixel_format
enums.doc: How a pixel of a frame for wguiWindowPresentPixels lies in memory: four bytes, 8 bits a channel.

entries.name: bgra8
entries.doc: Blue, green, red, alpha: 0xAARRGGBB read as a little-endian 32-bit number, which is how most software renderers keep their pixels.

entries.name: rgba8
entries.doc: Red, green, blue, alpha.

enums.name: pixel_alpha
enums.doc: What the fourth byte of a pixel means.

entries.name: opaque
entries.doc: Nothing: every pixel covers what is behind the window, whatever the byte holds.

entries.name: premultiplied
entries.doc: How much the pixel covers, with the colours already multiplied by it. Shows through only in a window made with WGUIWindowFlags_Transparent, on hosts that have such windows.

entries.name: straight
entries.doc: How much the pixel covers, with the colours as they are.

bitflags.name: event_class
bitflags.doc: Groups of events, for choosing which ones an instance queues. An event's class is the high byte of its type: the bit for it is 1 << (type >> 8).

entries.name: system
entries.doc: Lost events and completed requests. Always on.

entries.name: raw
entries.doc: Device input before the window system shapes it. Off unless asked for.

entries.name: gesture
entries.doc: Reserved.

entries.name: drop
entries.doc: Reserved.

entries.name: device
entries.doc: Reserved.

entries.name: gamepad
entries.doc: Reserved.

entries.name: default
entries.doc: What WGUI_INSTANCE_DESCRIPTOR_INIT asks for.

bitflags.name: window_flags
bitflags.doc: A window's state. The low 16 bits can be asked for (at creation and with wguiWindowSetFlags); the rest are only reported.

entries.name: visible
entries.doc: Shown on screen.

entries.name: resizable
entries.doc: The user can resize it.

entries.name: decorated
entries.doc: It has a title bar and borders.

entries.name: transparent
entries.doc: The window's background can show what is behind it. Only at creation.

entries.name: requestable
entries.doc: Every bit a program can ask for.

entries.name: focused
entries.doc: It has keyboard focus. Changes are announced by WGUIEventType_WindowFocusGained and WindowFocusLost, not by WindowFlagsChanged.

entries.name: hovered
entries.doc: The mouse cursor is over it. Changes are announced by the mouse's WGUIEventType_PointerEnter and PointerLeave.

entries.name: occluded
entries.doc: Nothing of it can be seen: drawing is wasted.

entries.name: fullscreen
entries.doc: Changed with wguiWindowSetFullscreen.

entries.name: logical_units
entries.doc: The descriptor's sizes, limits and position are in logical units: the host multiplies them by the scale factor of the display the window opens on, which the program cannot know yet.

entries.name: positioned
entries.doc: Place the window at the descriptor's x and y.

entries.name: no_deferral
entries.doc: Fail with WGUIStatus_Denied instead of waiting for a user gesture.

bitflags.name: wait_reasons
bitflags.doc: Why wguiInstanceWaitEvents returned. None of them: the timeout passed.

entries.name: events
entries.doc: The queue has records.

entries.name: woken
entries.doc: wguiInstanceWake was called.

entries.name: interrupted
entries.doc: The host ended the wait so that the system can reach the thread. Nothing happened; wait again.

entries.name: synthetic
entries.doc: Made by the host to keep the program's view consistent (a key release on focus loss), not caused by the user just now.

entries.name: coalesced
entries.doc: Stands for several events of the same kind that the host merged.

bitflags.name: modifiers
bitflags.doc: Modifier keys. The low bits say what is in effect, whichever key causes it (sticky keys count); the high bits say which keys are held, where the host can tell. AltGraph is reported as AltGraph, not as Control and Alt.

entries.name: super
entries.doc: The Windows key, Command on a Mac.

entries.name: caps_lock
entries.doc: Caps Lock is on.

entries.name: repeat
entries.doc: The key is being held: this press repeats the last one, with no release in between.

entries.name: composing
entries.doc: An input method took this key for the text it is composing.

entries.name: primary
entries.doc: The mouse cursor, the first finger down, or the pen. A program that handles one pointer handles the records with this flag.

entries.name: in_contact
entries.doc: A button is held, the finger touches, the pen's tip is down.

entries.name: has_pressure
entries.doc: The pressure field is measured, not assumed.

entries.name: has_tilt
entries.doc: The tilt and twist fields are measured.

bitflags.name: pointer_buttons
bitflags.doc: The buttons held: bit n - 1 for WGUIPointerButton n.

entries.name: momentum
entries.doc: The fingers have left the touchpad: the scroll is coasting.

entries.name: inverted
entries.doc: The user's "natural scrolling" setting is on. The deltas already follow it.

entries.name: completion
entries.doc: Suggestions are welcome.

entries.name: hidden_text
entries.doc: The field does not show what is typed.

entries.name: sensitive_data
entries.doc: Do not learn from or store what is typed.

entries.name: latin
entries.doc: Prefer a Latin layout.

entries.name: multiline
entries.doc: Enter inserts a line break.

entries.name: active
entries.doc: An input method is attached to the window.

entries.name: from_key
entries.doc: This text is what the key event just before it produced. A program that already used that event's text must not insert it again.

entries.name: continues
entries.doc: The text was too long for one record: the next record of this type continues it.

entries.name: owned
entries.doc: This instance wrote the current content.

entries.name: has_text
entries.doc: There is text. Not set when the host cannot tell without a request.

entries.name: needs_request
entries.doc: Reading will answer WGUIStatus_Pending until a request completes.

bitflags.name: default_actions
bitflags.doc: The embedder's own reactions to input.

entries.name: keys
entries.doc: Keys pressed without Control, Alt or Super: scrolling with the space bar and the arrows, moving focus with Tab.

entries.name: shortcuts
entries.doc: Key combinations the embedder lets a page take (save, print, find). Others (closing the tab) cannot be prevented.

entries.name: wheel
entries.doc: Scrolling and zooming the page.

entries.name: touch_gestures
entries.doc: Panning and zooming the page by touch.

entries.name: default
entries.doc: What a new window prevents.

structs.name: rect
structs.doc: A rectangle in a window, in physical pixels from the content area's top-left corner.

members.name: abi_version
members.doc: The version of the header the program was built with. Leave it as the INIT macro sets it.

members.name: event_mask
members.doc: The classes of events to queue. See wguiInstanceSetEventMask.

members.name: required_features
members.doc: Features the program cannot do without.

members.name: application_id
members.doc: A stable name for the program, such as "org.example.editor". Window systems use it to group windows and to find the program's icon and name.

members.name: abi_version
members.doc: The newest version the host implements.

members.name: shortcut_modifier
members.doc: The modifier this platform's shortcuts use: Control, or Super on a Mac.

members.name: input_devices
members.doc: The input hardware the host knows of. A keyboard missing here is the reason to show an on-screen one.

members.name: max_cursor_size
members.doc: The largest width or height a custom cursor may have, in pixels. 0 if unknown.

members.name: x
members.doc: The display's top-left corner on the desktop.

members.name: work_x
members.doc: The part of the display windows can use: without docks, panels and menu bars.

members.name: scale_factor
members.doc: Physical pixels per logical unit.

members.name: refresh_rate
members.doc: In thousandths of a hertz. 0 if unknown.

members.name: target
members.doc: The name of a target the embedder provides (a canvas, a view) for the window to adopt. Empty is the embedder's default target. Naming a target does not need WGUIFeatureName_TopLevelWindows; a target already adopted answers WGUIStatus_Busy.

members.name: flags
members.doc: The requestable flags to start with.

members.name: width
members.doc: The size of the content area. 0 lets the host choose. An adopted target keeps its own size.

members.name: min_width
members.doc: Limits, as in wguiWindowSetSizeLimits.

members.name: x
members.doc: Used with WGUIWindowOptions_Positioned.

members.name: display
members.doc: The display to open on. 0 lets the host choose.

members.name: width
members.doc: The size of the content area: what a surface on the window should be configured with.

members.name: scale_factor
members.doc: Physical pixels per logical unit, for sizing text and controls.

members.name: x
members.doc: The content area's top-left corner on the desktop, or WGUI_POSITION_UNDEFINED.

members.name: frame_left
members.doc: How far the window's borders and title bar reach beyond the content area.

members.name: safe_left
members.doc: How much of the content area's edges may be covered by notches, rounded corners or system bars.

members.name: display
members.doc: The display most of the window is on, or 0.

members.name: cursor_grab
members.doc: The grab in effect now, which may be less than what was asked for.

members.name: serial
members.doc: Goes up whenever anything in this struct changes.

members.name: display
members.doc: The display to cover. 0 is the one the window is on.

members.name: width
members.doc: The image's size in pixels.

members.name: hotspot_x
members.doc: The pixel that points.

members.name: scale_factor
members.doc: How many image pixels make one logical unit: 2 for an image drawn for a display of scale factor 2.

members.name: pixels
members.doc: RGBA, 8 bits each, alpha not premultiplied, rows from the top, no padding.

members.name: pixels_size
members.doc: width * height * 4.

structs.name: pixel_frame
structs.doc: A frame for wguiWindowPresentPixels: rows of pixels from the top, each row from the left.

members.name: width
members.doc: The frame's size in pixels.

members.name: stride
members.doc: Bytes from the start of one row to the start of the next. 0 means width * 4: no padding.

members.name: pixels_size
members.doc: How much of `pixels` may be read: at least stride * (height - 1) + width * 4.

members.name: cursor_area
members.doc: Where the caret is, so the input method can put its candidate window next to it.

members.name: input_area
members.doc: The whole text field, so an on-screen keyboard can avoid covering it. Zero size if unknown.

members.name: sequence
members.doc: Goes up whenever the content changes, as far as the host notices.

structs.name: clipboard_item
structs.doc: One representation of what is being copied.

members.name: mime_type
members.doc: "text/plain" for UTF-8 text.

event_header.doc: What every event record starts with. Records are little-endian, 8-byte aligned, and say how long they are: a record a program does not know, or one longer than it expects, is stepped over by its size.

members.name: size
members.doc: The whole record in bytes, strings and padding included; a multiple of 8. The next record starts this far on.

members.name: window
members.doc: The window the event is for, or 0.

members.name: timestamp
members.doc: When it happened, in nanoseconds on the clock of wguiInstanceGetTime. Never decreases from one record to the next.

members.name: device
members.doc: Which piece of hardware, where the host can tell them apart; 0 otherwise.

members.name: sequence
members.doc: Counts the records this instance has been given.

event_records.name: events_lost_event
event_records.doc: The queue overflowed and records were dropped. What follows makes the program's view right again: releases for keys and buttons it believes held, and each window's current size and flags. Dropped text is gone.

members.name: count
members.doc: How many records were dropped.

members.name: classes
members.doc: The classes they belonged to.

event_records.name: request_completed_event
event_records.doc: A request made with a tag is over. Every accepted request gets exactly one, also when its window is destroyed first.

members.name: tag
members.doc: The tag the program passed.

event_records.name: window_resized_event
event_records.doc: The window's content area has a new size or scale factor. A surface on it should be configured again with this size.

members.name: flags
members.doc: All of the window's flags now.

members.name: changed
members.doc: The ones that differ from before.

members.name: grab
members.doc: The grab in effect now.

event_records.name: key_event
event_records.doc:
A key went down or up.

Per window, downs and ups pair up: no release arrives for a press the window did not get. A held key repeats as further downs flagged Repeat. Before a window loses focus it gets a synthetic release for every key still down.

`text` is what the press types through the keyboard layout, with or without text input on. While text input is on, the same text also arrives as a WGUIEventType_TextCommit flagged FromKey.

members.name: physical_key
members.doc: Which key, wherever the layout puts its letters.

members.name: native_scancode
members.doc: The platform's own code for the key, for keys physicalKey cannot name. 0 if unknown.

members.name: key
members.doc: What the key means with the modifiers held, Control aside.

members.name: key_unmodified
members.doc: What it means with no modifier held: the layout's base layer. 0 if unknown.

members.name: modifiers
members.doc: The modifiers after this event.

members.name: key_string
members.doc: `key` as text when it is a character, a dead key or a sequence.

members.name: text
members.doc: The text this press types. Absent for releases and for keys that type nothing.

members.name: text_with_all_modifiers
members.doc: The same with Control applied too, as terminals want it (Control+C is U+0003).

event_records.name: modifiers_changed_event
event_records.doc: The modifiers changed. Follows the key event that caused it, and focus gained when some are already held.

members.name: keyboard_area
members.doc: The part of the window an on-screen keyboard covers. Zero size if none.

event_records.name: text_composition_event
event_records.doc: The text being composed by an input method: it replaces the composition shown so far, and empty text ends it. Draw it at the caret, marked as unfinished; it is not part of the document.

members.name: selection_start
members.doc: The input method's cursor or selection inside the text, as byte offsets, or WGUI_NO_TEXT_CURSOR.

event_records.name: text_commit_event
event_records.doc: Text to insert at the caret. Ends the composition, if there is one. While text input is on, every insertion arrives this way, typed keys included.

event_records.name: pointer_event
event_records.doc:
A mouse cursor, a finger or a pen did something over a window.

Every press and every release is its own Down or Up. From a Down until the pointer's last button is up, its events go to that window even when it moves outside. Cancel means all of that pointer's buttons are up and the gesture should be undone.

members.name: button
members.doc: The button that went down or up.

members.name: buttons
members.doc: The buttons held after this event.

members.name: x
members.doc: Position in the window.

members.name: delta_x
members.doc: Movement since this pointer's previous record. With the cursor locked this is all that changes.

members.name: pressure
members.doc: 0 to 1. Without WGUIPointerFlags_HasPressure: 0.5 in contact, else 0.

members.name: tangential_pressure
members.doc: A pen's barrel pressure, -1 to 1.

members.name: tilt_x
members.doc: Degrees from upright, -90 to 90.

members.name: twist
members.doc: Degrees of rotation about the pen's axis, 0 to 360.

members.name: contact_width
members.doc: The size of the contact, in physical pixels. 0 if unknown.

members.name: click_count
members.doc: For a Down or Up: 2 for a double click, as the system counts them. 0 if unknown.

event_records.name: wheel_event
event_records.doc: A wheel turned or a touchpad scrolled. Positive deltaY scrolls the content up, showing what is below; positive deltaX shows what is to the right.

members.name: x
members.doc: Where the cursor is.

event_records.name: raw_motion_event
event_records.doc: A mouse moved, as the device reports it: no acceleration, no window.

events.name: app_suspended
events.doc: The program is no longer in front of the user (a phone's home screen, a hidden tab). Its windows may be unusable until it resumes.

events.name: app_quit_requested
events.doc: The user asked the whole program to quit. It decides whether to.

events.name: app_terminating
events.doc: The program is about to be stopped whatever it does. Save now.

events.name: app_theme_changed
events.doc: The system switched between light and dark.

events.name: displays_changed
events.doc: A display was added, removed or changed. List them again.

events.name: window_focus_lost
events.doc: Comes after the synthetic releases of the keys that were down.

events.name: window_close_requested
events.doc: The user asked to close the window. Nothing has happened to it: the program destroys it, or asks the user first, or carries on.

events.name: window_redraw_requested
events.doc: The window should be drawn again: the program asked with wguiWindowRequestRedraw, or the system uncovered it. A new window is not asked: its first WGUIEventType_WindowResized is when to draw it for the first time.

events.name: window_lost
events.doc: The window's host side is gone (the embedder removed its target). The handle only remains to be destroyed.
